steps: Bring at least 4 cups of water to the boil on high heat. Add the noodles and stir for 30-60 seconds so they don't stick, then cover and return to the boil (about 3 minutes).

Meanwhile, gently wash the mushrooms and vegetables. Trim the roots off the enoki and separate them.
Slice the shiitake, king oyster mushrooms, carrot, broccoli, celery and red pepper into thin 1-2 inch strips. Cut the green onion to the same length and mince the garlic.

Add the carrots, potato and water.
Seal and pressure cook on High for 4 minutes, then quick release the pressure.
Stir in the coconut milk and serve.

recipe.name: Chestnut Cake with Chocolate Chips
recipe.notes: No bundt pan? Use a 21 cm round cake pan and start checking with a skewer after about 35 minutes. Serves 4 to 6.

Grease a small bundt pan (about 1 litre capacity) with non-stick spray, dust generously with flour and tap out the excess.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff peaks form.
In a separate bowl, beat the egg yolks, chestnut purée and butter until smooth.
Fold through the flour, baking powder and salt.
Gently fold in the egg whites a third at a time, taking care not to lose too much air, then fold through the chocolate chips.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan, leaving at least 2 cm space from the rim.
Bake for 40-50 minutes, until a skewer inserted in the middle comes out clean.
Cool in the pan on a wire rack for about 15 minutes, then gently unmould and leave to cool completely.

recipe.name: Sweet and Spicy Gochujang Chicken

Add the water and knead with your hands into a smooth, oily dough.
Roll the dough into a log, cut into 26 pieces and roll each into a ball, then flatten into a 4-inch circle.
Fill each wrapper with 1 tbsp filling, fold over and pinch to seal, then pleat the edges with your thumb.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a large pan over medium heat until bubbles form around a chopstick.
Fry 5–6 puffs at a time for about 2 minutes per side until golden. Drain on a wire rack or paper towels.

recipe.name: Chinese Meat Pies (Xian Bing)
recipe.notes: The dough should be soft but not overly sticky; adjust water to your flour. Cook in 2–3 batches. Flattened uncooked pies freeze for up to 2 months — fry from frozen, covered, over medium-low heat.

Meanwhile, combine all the filling ingredients and stir in one direction with chopsticks until sticky.
Flatten a dough ball into a disc about ½ cm thick. Place ⅛ of the filling in the centre, pleat the edges around it and seal tightly at the top. Place on an oiled tray and repeat.
Heat enough oil to coat a heavy skillet. Add the pies, seam side down, and flatten to about 2.5 cm thick.
Fry over low heat until golden underneath, then flip, cover and fry until the other side browns. Flip once more to re-crisp the first side for about 20 seconds.

Spoon the boba into a glass and drizzle the syrup down the inside walls.
Fill with ice, pour in the matcha, then the milk. Stir and serve.

recipe.name: Lamb Pulao
recipe.notes: Any bone-in cut such as leg or shoulder works. Broth can be made in an Instant Pot: pressure cook on High for 20–22 minutes, using only 2¾ cups water. Adjust broth to your usual rice-to-water ratio.

Sprinkle with cilantro and mint, fluff gently and serve with raita or plain yogurt.

recipe.name: Instant Pot Pho Ga (Vietnamese Chicken Noodle Soup)
recipe.notes: Total time about 1 hr 25 min. Star anise is deliberately left out so it doesn't overpower the clean broth.

recipe.name: Thai Banana Pancakes (Banana Roti)
recipe.notes: Use bananas with a hint of green; overripe ones turn mushy. You can swap the condensed milk in the dough for 1 tbsp sugar.
prePrep: Whisk the salt into the water until dissolved, then whisk in the condensed milk and egg. Rub the butter into the flour, add to the liquid and knead briefly into a shaggy dough. Rest 15-30 minutes.

Knead for about 5 minutes until evenly moist and tacky, then rest 10-15 minutes. Cut into 80g pieces (about 11), shape into balls, brush generously with the melted butter and oil mixture and rest at least 3 hours (or refrigerate overnight; bring back to room temperature for 2 hours).

Leave to stand for 5 minutes before serving.

steps: Soak the cloud ear fungus and the shiitake mushrooms in separate bowls of warm water until rehydrated. Drain, snip the tough stems off the fungus and tear it into bite-sized pieces.

Debone the drumsticks: cut through the meat to expose the bone, crack the bone near the bottom with the back of a cleaver, then pull the meat away. Cut into large chunks (or keep bone-in and cut each into 3-4 pieces).
Mix the marinade oyster sauce, light soy sauce, cooking wine, cornstarch and white pepper, pour over the chicken and massage in.
In a bowl, mix the sauce ingredients: oyster sauce, light and dark soy sauce, cooking wine, salt and sugar. In another bowl, mix the cornstarch and water for the slurry.
Heat a wok on high until smoking, then add a third of the oil. Reduce to low, add the ginger for 10-15 seconds, then the garlic and shallots for 15-20 seconds until fragrant.
Increase to medium, spread the chicken out and sear without stirring for about 1 minute. Flip and cook for 30-40 seconds.
Make a space in the centre, add the mushrooms with another third of the oil and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute, then stir everything together for 20-30 seconds.
Add the Chinese sausage, cloud ear fungus and stir-frying wine and stir for 15-20 seconds. Pour in the sauce while stirring, then add the hot water.
Bring to a boil on high, then cover and cook for 1.5-2 minutes on medium. Reduce to low, taste and adjust, adding the finishing sugar.
Stir in the slurry over low heat until thickened, then drizzle in the sesame oil and add the green onion whites.
Heat a clay pot with its lid on over low heat, add the remaining oil and, once smoking, transfer in the contents of the wok and cover.
Increase to high. Once steam appears (30-40 seconds), drizzle the finishing wine around the edge of the lid, cook for 30 seconds more until bubbling, then turn off the heat and serve from the pot.

recipe.name: Tuna Pasta Bake

Boil water in a kettle, pour it into a saucepan with 0.5 tsp salt and cook the carrots.

Layer the pasta in a tray, add the chopped vegetables, tuna and sweetcorn, then pour in the cooked sauce and toss until evenly coated.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes.
Stir the pasta thoroughly, sprinkle over the cheese and bake for a further 30 minutes.

recipe.name: Vegan Bao Buns with Pulled Jackfruit
recipe.notes: The buns can be made 1 day ahead.
steps: Combine the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a bowl. Add about 120 ml warm water and 1.5 tbsp oil, mix roughly with a wooden spoon, then bring together by hand, adding 2-3 more tablespoons of water one at a time until the dough is neither dry nor sticky.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Form into a ball, rub with a little oil, cover with a towel and leave somewhere warm for 1-2 hours, until doubled.
Cut baking paper circles to line the steamer and pierce them with lots of small holes. Cut eight 5 cm squares of baking paper.
Tip the dough onto a lightly floured surface, press out the air and divide into 8 balls. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll each ball into a 0.5 cm thick oval, fold in half with a square of paper (or a little oil) between the halves.
Place the buns in the lined steamer and prove for another 30 minutes. If the steamer is small, rest the rest on a lightly floured lined tray.

Set the steamer over a half-filled pot of water on medium-high heat without peeking. Once the water simmers vigorously, steam for 10 minutes, then take off the heat and rest for 5 minutes before lifting the lid. Repeat with any remaining buns.
Drain the jackfruit, cut off the firm pointy ends and squash each piece gently so it separates into strands.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a medium pan and fry the spring onions until soft. Add the garlic and ginger and fry gently until fragrant, then add the five spice and fry for 1 minute.
Add the tamari, hoisin, rice vinegar and sugar and stir until the sugar melts. Add the jackfruit and mix well to warm through and soak up the sauce.
Fill each bun with pulled jackfruit, fresh veg, herbs, chilli, crushed peanuts and extra hoisin.

recipe.name: Tomato Tofu Soup
recipe.notes: Use medium firm or firmer tofu; silken or soft tofu will fall apart.
steps: Dice some of the tomatoes into small pieces and cut the rest into larger pieces. If you want to remove the skins, score them, pour boiling water over, leave for about 20 seconds, then peel.
Dice the mushrooms. Chop the spring onions, separating the white parts from the greens. Slice and smash the ginger.
Rinse the tofu and cut it into 32-40 medium pieces.
Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat lightly, leaving some white and yolk separate.
Mix the cornstarch with 4 tbsp water until smooth to make a slurry.
Heat a wok on high for 20-30 seconds, add the cooking oil and heat for 15-20 seconds, then add the ginger. Once the oil is rippling, turn the heat down.
Sauté the white parts of the spring onion, then add the small diced tomatoes and cook for 20-30 seconds. Add the larger tomato pieces and cook for another 30 seconds.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 20-30 seconds, then transfer everything to a large pot.
Add the chicken broth and water, cover and simmer for a minute and a half.
Add the tofu, cover and boil for 10 minutes, then turn the heat down to low.
Stir the slurry again and slowly pour it in while stirring the soup, adding more for a thicker consistency. Turn the heat back to high.
Slowly pour in the eggs while gently stirring. Once they float to the surface, add the ketchup, salt, sugar and sesame oil.
Taste and adjust, then serve in a large bowl garnished with the spring onion greens.

recipe.name: No-Bake Matcha Bars
steps: Pit and soak the dates, then blend to a paste in a food processor.
Add everything else and pulse until well combined but still textured.
Press evenly into a parchment-lined dish to your preferred thickness.
Press extra Lil Bucks gently into the top.
Freeze for at least an hour, then slice with a pizza cutter.

recipe.name: Pistachio Sponge Cake
recipe.notes: Cake flour gives the softest, cotton-like texture.
steps: Preheat the oven to 150°C (300°F). Grease and line a 7 x 7 inch pan with parchment.
Mix the egg yolks and 60g sugar until the sugar has almost dissolved. Add the oil and milk and mix until combined.
Sift in the flour and ground pistachios and whisk in a circular motion until no flour remains.
In another bowl, whisk the egg whites with the cream of tartar until bubbly, then gradually add the 75g sugar and whisk to stiff peaks.
Gently whisk the meringue into the batter in a few batches, just until combined.
Pour into the pan and draw a skewer through the batter in both directions to release air pockets.
Bake at 150°C for 30 minutes, then lower to 140°C (285°F) for 35 minutes.
Cool completely, then slice horizontally into 3 layers.
For the frosting, soften the cream cheese in a chilled bowl, then mix in the powdered sugar and vanilla. Add the whipping cream and whisk just to stiff peaks.
Layer the sponge with the frosting and dust with ground pistachios.

recipe.name: Simple Healthy Slaw
recipe.notes: Best the day it's made but keeps several days covered in the fridge.

Toast the seeds in a small skillet over medium heat, stirring often, until fragrant and the pepitas start to pop. Add to the bowl and toss.
Whisk the olive oil, 2 tbsp lemon juice, garlic, cumin and salt until blended.
Drizzle the dressing over the slaw and toss to coat. Add another tablespoon of lemon juice if needed.
Serve immediately or cover and refrigerate for up to several hours.

yellow bell pepper, cut into small cubes
tinned black beans, drained and rinsed
salt and freshly ground black pepper

recipe.name: One-Pot Mexican Chicken and Rice
recipe.notes: If the rice starts sticking before it's cooked, add a splash of water or stock.
steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan, add the chicken and stir for 5 minutes until coloured all over.
Add the garlic, peppers, cumin, chilli and paprika and stir for 1–2 minutes until everything is coated in the spices.
Add the rice, passata, stock, black beans and seasoning and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 15–20 minutes until the rice is cooked and the liquid absorbed.
Stir in the sweetcorn and heat through for 4–5 minutes.
Top with the cheese and grill for about 5 minutes until melted. Sprinkle with spring onion and serve.

recipe.name: Ferrero Rocher Milkshake
recipe.notes: Amounts are per person; multiply for more servings.
steps: Add the Nutella, peanut butter, milk and ice cream to a blender.

recipe.name: Yin Yang Fried Rice
steps: Wash the rice 3 times in clean water, then cook it with the 13 oz water in a rice cooker.
Separate the eggs into yolks and whites. Quarter the tomato, discard the stem, dice the core and cut the rest half into strips and half diced. Cut half the onion into strips and dice the rest.
Halve the shrimp lengthwise. Halve the chicken breast horizontally, slice into short strips and marinate with the salt, cornstarch and water.
For the red sauce, mix the ketchup, sugar, vinegar, salt and chicken broth in a bowl. Taste and adjust.
Fold a piece of foil at least 1.5 times the width of your serving dish in half lengthwise and curve it into an S shape. Mix the egg yolks into the cooked rice.
Heat the wok on the highest heat for about a minute, add 1 tbsp oil and fry the rice for about 3 minutes. Season with salt, cook for 30-40 seconds more, then spread level on the serving plate.

Reheat the wok for 30 seconds, add 1 tbsp oil and stir-fry the chicken for 30-40 seconds. Push it aside, add the sliced onion, then the diced tomato (pressing out the juice) and the tomato strips, and stir-fry for 40-50 seconds.
Add the red sauce, lower the heat and adjust to taste. Stir in a slurry of the cornstarch and water, cook for another minute, then transfer to a bowl.
Clean the wok, heat on high for a minute and add 2 tbsp oil. Add the shrimp, turn the heat to low and cook for 20 seconds. Add the diced onion for 20 seconds, then the chicken broth and salt.

Beat the egg whites until airy. Stir in a slurry of the cornstarch and water, then pour the egg whites slowly in a circle over the surface without stirring. Cook for 20-30 seconds and turn off the heat.
Add 1 tsp oil for shine and stir in the peas.
Set the foil mould on the rice, spoon the red sauce on one side and the white sauce on the other, then lift the mould straight up to serve.

recipe.name: Chicken Dumplings
steps: Fry the onion in oil, then add the garlic, salt and black pepper and cook until the onion is soft.
Add the chicken, mix into the onions and cook for 5 minutes until no longer pink.
Add the cabbage, then the carrots, and cook until the veg is soft, stirring often to avoid sticking.
Mix in the fish sauce, chilli powder, chives, spring onions and light soy sauce and cook for 5 minutes.
Fill the gyoza wrappers with the filling.
Fry the gyoza in shallow oil until brown on one side, then flip.
Add a splash of water and steam until the wrappers turn translucent.

recipe.name: Cantonese Chicken Chow Mein
recipe.notes: Steaming before boiling keeps the noodles from going soggy. For a vegetarian version, use mushrooms or firm tofu and vegetarian oyster sauce and bouillon.
steps: Cut the red onion, carrot and cabbage into long, thin strips and the green onions into 1-inch pieces.
Debone the chicken thighs if needed, even out the thickness and cut into thin strips along the grain.
Mix the chicken with 1 tbsp oyster sauce, the cornstarch, water and white pepper until well coated. Set aside to marinate.
For the sauce, combine 2 tbsp oyster sauce, the light and dark soy sauces, sugar and chicken bouillon powder.

Steam the noodles over boiling water in a covered wok on high heat for 12-15 minutes, then drop them into the boiling water, loosen and cook for 5-6 minutes on medium-high until no pale dot remains in the centre. Drain.

Mix 1 tbsp oil into the chicken. Heat the wok on high until just smoking, add 2 tbsp oil, then lower to medium and spread the chicken out. Sear for 30-40 seconds, then stir-fry on high for 40-50 seconds until nearly cooked. Transfer to a dish.
In the residual oil, cook the red onion until aromatic, add the cabbage for 20-30 seconds, then the carrots for 30 seconds on high. Transfer to the dish with the chicken.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil and the noodles on high heat. Spread them out and sear for 1 minute, flip and sear another minute, then pan-fry on medium for 40 seconds.
Stir the sauce, turn the heat to low and pour it in, stirring to distribute.
Return the chicken and vegetables and stir-fry for 30 seconds. Turn up to medium-high, add the bean sprouts and stir-fry for about 1 minute.
Drizzle with sesame oil and stir-fry on high for about 1 minute, then serve.

recipe.notes: 2 black tea bags can replace the loose tea. Use less milk and more water for a lighter chai.

Add the milk and bring back to the boil over high heat.

Strain into cups and sweeten to taste.

recipe.name: Chilli Con Carne

steps: Heat the oil in a deep pan or wok over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft and slightly translucent.
Turn the heat up, add the minced beef and brown for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until crumbled and no longer pink.
Add the garlic, chilli powder, paprika and cumin. Stir and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Mix the chicken stock into the hot water and pour in with the chopped tomatoes. Add the herbs and sugar (or chocolate), season with salt and pepper, then stir in the tomato purée.
Bring to the boil, cover, then reduce to a gentle simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add a couple of tablespoons of water if it gets dry.
Stir in the kidney beans, bring to the boil and cook uncovered for another 10 minutes. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Replace the lid, turn off the heat and leave to stand for 10 minutes before serving.

recipe.name: Strawberry Cream Cake
recipe.notes: Pat the strawberry pieces dry on kitchen paper so they don't make the cream watery. For 3–4 thinner layers baked separately, bake 15–20 minutes.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (gas mark 4) and butter and line an 18cm cake tin. Warm the butter and milk together in a bowl over hot water.
Set the bowl of eggs over a pan of hot water, add the sugar and honey and stir until the sugar melts and the mixture reaches 40°C. Remove from the heat and add the vanilla.
Whip with a hand mixer on high for 2.5 minutes, medium for 2.5 minutes, then low for 1.5 minutes, until the batter falls in a thick ribbon.
Sift in the flour and fold gently from the bottom up until just combined.
Mix a little batter into the warm butter and milk, then fold it back into the rest evenly.

Whip the 300g cream; when it starts to thicken, add the strawberry jam and a little food colouring and whip to soft peaks.
Level the cake and slice into 3 layers. Place the first layer on a turntable, spread with jam and strawberry cream and press in the strawberry pieces.
Repeat with the second layer, top with the last layer and cover the top and sides with the remaining cream, smoothing with a straight spatula.
Chill the cake for a while. Whip the 60g cream with 6g sugar to 60–70% (pourable), pour over the top and let it flow slightly down the sides.
Decorate with strawberries and mint leaves, if using.

recipe.name: Scallion Pancakes (Cong You Bing)
recipe.notes: For thinner pancakes, cut the rope into 3 and roll each to about 23cm, cooking one at a time. Freeze uncooked pancakes between parchment and cook from frozen. Serve with a dip of chilli oil, black vinegar and light soy.

Brush with the filling paste and sprinkle over the scallions. Roll up loosely from the short side into a rope.

Heat the oil in a frying pan over high heat until a piece of scallion sizzles, then turn to medium and add the pancakes top-side down.
Cover and cook about 2 minutes until golden underneath, then flip and cook covered until the second side is golden.
Rest on a wire rack for a minute or two before serving warm.

recipe.name: Mary Berry's Fish Pie
recipe.notes: Make ahead: cover the assembled pie with foil and chill for up to 36 hours, then bake at 200C for about 40 minutes until piping hot. To freeze, leave out the eggs. Floury potatoes such as Maris Piper or King Edward make the best mash.

Uncover and increase the heat to drive off any moisture. Sprinkle in the flour, then add the milk gradually, stirring well between additions, and let the sauce thicken.

Pour into the buttered dish, leave to cool and top with the hard-boiled eggs.

Spread the mash over the filling and score with a fork.
Bake for about 30 minutes until the potato is crisp and golden-brown. Serve with garlic bread.

Add the soy sauces, oyster sauce, honey, sesame oil, Shaoxing wine, ginger and garlic powder and massage into the wings. Marinate for at least 15 minutes, or overnight for best flavour.
Spray the air fryer basket with oil and arrange the wings in a single layer without overlapping, in batches if needed.
Air fry at 400F for 8 minutes, flip and air fry for another 4-5 minutes until cooked through (165F inside).
Garnish with green onion, if using.

Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt, then divide between the tins.

steps: Pulse the onion, garlic and ginger in a food processor until finely chopped.

recipe.name: Jaffna Lamb Curry
recipe.notes: The spice mix makes more than needed; store the rest airtight in a cool dark place for up to 2 months. The curry freezes well in portions — reheat gently, covered, with a splash of water.
steps: For the Jaffna spice mix, toast all the spice-mix ingredients except the chilli flakes and curry leaves (and ground fenugreek, if using) in a dry pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until fragrant.
Cool, then grind to a fine powder in a small food processor with the reserved ingredients. Set aside.
Trim excess fat from the lamb, cut into 3–4 cm chunks and season.

Add the onion and cook for 12–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden.

Increase to high heat and add the garlic and ginger paste, lemongrass and lamb. Once sealed on all sides, add 2 tbsp of the spice mix, the chilli powder, turmeric and tomato purée and fry for 2 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low, cover and cook for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the coconut milk and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until rich and thickened. Season to taste and serve with rice or roti.

recipe.name: Matcha Butter Cookies
steps: Sift the flour, matcha and salt together into a small bowl.
In a stand mixer, beat the butter and sugar on medium until creamy and pale, then add the egg and mix until fully incorporated.
Lower the speed and gradually add the flour mixture until just combined; the dough will be firm.
Chill the dough for 10 minutes. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line two baking trays with parchment.
Press cookies onto the trays with a cookie press, 2 cm apart. Alternatively, pipe with a large open-star tip or roll into 1.5 cm balls.

recipe.name: Dairy-Free Tangzhong Bread
recipe.notes: Proving the bowl in a sink of warm water helps the dough rise faster. Keep the dough slightly sticky; avoid adding too much flour.
steps: Make the tangzhong: in a non-stick pan, mix 35 g bread flour with the water. Stir over medium heat until it becomes a smooth, thick paste that still slides out of the pan.
Transfer the tangzhong to a dish, cover and cool to room temperature.
Warm the oat milk until lukewarm. Make sure the butter and egg are at room temperature so the yeast activates.
In a large bowl, mix the bread flour, sugar, salt and yeast. Add the egg, lukewarm oat milk, butter and the tangzhong (about 155 g) and mix into a sticky ball of dough.
Knead by hand for 15–30 minutes (or 15 minutes on medium in a stand mixer, then briefly by hand) until smooth, elastic and only slightly tacky. Use no more than 2–3 tbsp flour.
Place in a greased bowl, cover and leave somewhere warm for about 1.5 hours (up to 2–3 hours) until doubled.
Divide the dough into 3 equal balls. Roll each into a long oval with a rolling pin, then roll up and fit side by side in a lined or greased loaf pan.
Cover and prove somewhere warm for 45–60 minutes until the dough rises a little above the pan.
Whisk the egg with the oat milk and brush over the dough.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) on the second-lowest rack for 25–27 minutes until golden brown. Turn out and cool on a wire rack.

recipe.name: Lemon Drizzle Cake

Add the butter and knead on speed 2 for 2-3 minutes, then speed 4 for about 5 minutes until soft, smooth, elastic and passing the windowpane test. If firm, add milk a teaspoon at a time.
Cover in a lightly oiled bowl and leave in a warm place for 45 minutes to 1 hour until doubled.
Knock back, divide into 9 equal pieces and roll into balls. Cover and rest for 5 minutes.
Roll each ball into a rectangle about 6 x 4 inches. Put about 1 tbsp kaya near the top, fold the top over to enclose it, fold in the sides and pinch to seal.
Cut the remaining dough into strips with a pizza cutter, roll the dough down into an oval bun and place in the pan. Repeat with the rest.
Cover and proof in a warm place for 45 minutes to 1 hour until very puffy. Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F) for the last 10 minutes.
Brush with egg wash and bake in the middle of the oven for 15 minutes until golden brown (88°C in the centre).
Cool on a rack to warm or room temperature before serving.

recipe.name: Microwave Jacket Potatoes
steps: Wash the potatoes and prick the skins all over with a fork.
Put them on a microwave-safe plate lined with kitchen roll and cover with another sheet.
Microwave for 4 minutes, turn over (careful, they're hot), re-cover and cook for another 4 minutes, then turn again.
Keep cooking in 1-2 minute bursts until soft all the way through and the skins are wrinkled. Leave to cool slightly.
Heat the oven to 220C/200C fan/gas 7. Rub the skins with the olive oil and sprinkle with sea salt.
Bake for 10-15 minutes until the skins start to crisp. Split open, add butter and serve with your favourite toppings.

recipe.name: Korean Bulgogi Chicken Wings
steps: In a large bowl, toss the wings with the seasoning: 1 tbsp soy sauce, black pepper, 2 tsp garlic, ginger powder and onion powder.
Spread the potato starch on a tray or in a zip-lock bag and coat the wings evenly.
To air fry: arrange the wings in a single layer in the air fryer basket (in batches if needed) and cook at 400°F for 8 minutes per side, 16 minutes in total.
To deep fry instead: heat 2 cups of neutral oil in a large pan or Dutch oven to 350°F and fry the wings for 7–8 minutes until golden and cooked through to 165°F.
In a small bowl, combine the honey, brown sugar, remaining soy sauce, sesame seeds, sesame oil and remaining garlic.
Pour the sauce over the fried wings, toss to coat and garnish with green onion.

recipe.name: Pistachio Cake with Orange Blossom Icing
recipe.notes: Total time about 2 hr 10 min including cooling. All-purpose flour gives a denser cake than cake-and-pastry flour.
steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F) with a rack in the centre. Line four 8-9 inch foil cake pans with parchment and spray with flour-based baking spray.
Process the pistachios with the 90g flour and 1/4 tsp salt until finely ground. Sift into a bowl, regrinding any coarse pieces.
Beat the egg whites on medium-high until foamy, about 2 minutes, then gradually add half the sugar and beat to medium-stiff peaks, 3-4 minutes more.
In a very large bowl, beat the yolks with the remaining sugar until pale and thick, 3-4 minutes. Beat in the vanilla, orange zest and food colouring.
Fold a third of the whites into the yolks until no streaks remain, then gently fold in the rest. Fold in the pistachio mixture in thirds; the batter should look fluffy like meringue.
Divide between the pans, smooth the tops and bake for 18-20 minutes until golden and a tester comes out clean. Cool completely on a rack, about 1 hour.

For the icing, combine the 128g sugar and 37g flour in a saucepan over medium heat. Gradually whisk in the milk and keep whisking for 2-4 minutes until thick like pudding. Transfer to a bowl, cover the surface with plastic wrap and cool to room temperature, about 1 hour.
Beat the butter on high until fluffy, 1 minute. Beat in the cooled mixture 1 tbsp at a time until stiff peaks form, then beat in the orange blossom water and salt.
Place one layer on a cake stand, spread with 3/4 cup icing to the edge and repeat with the remaining layers.
Spread the remaining icing very thinly over the top and sides, scraping off excess for a naked look.

recipe.name: Lavender Earl Grey Shortbread Cookies
recipe.notes: Allow about 1.5 hours extra for chilling and setting.
steps: Cream the butter and sugar. Add the salt, the tea leaves from the tea bag and the milk powder, then mix in the flour and 1 tbsp of the lavender to form a thick dough.
Place the dough between two sheets of plastic wrap and roll to about ¼ inch thick, folding the edges in. Chill for at least 30 minutes.
Remove the top wrap, sprinkle with the remaining ½ tbsp lavender, cover and press it in lightly with a rolling pin. Chill for another 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment or a baking mat.
Cut the dough into squares or shapes and place about 4 inches apart.
Bake for about 15 minutes until the edges are just turning brown. Cool completely on the sheet before moving, as they break easily.
Mix the powdered sugar and milk into a thick glaze (add some tea leaves if you like), drizzle over the cooled cookies and let set for about 1 hour.

recipe.name: Moroccan Jackfruit 'Lamb' with Lemon Couscous
steps: Drain, rinse and pat dry the jackfruit, then cut into 1 inch chunks. Drain, rinse and pat dry the chickpeas.

Add the garlic, ginger and coriander stalks and stir for 1 minute. Add the jackfruit and stir for 3-4 minutes.
Add the ras el hanout and stir for 2 minutes until the jackfruit is well coated and taking on the colour of the spices.
Stir in the tomato purée for 30 seconds, then the mint sauce for 30 seconds.
Add the chopped tomatoes, stir, turn up the heat and simmer to thicken for 10 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and maple syrup and squeeze in the lemon juice. Turn the heat down and simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally so it doesn't catch.

Meanwhile, halve the preserved lemon and put it in a mixing bowl with the extra virgin olive oil, cumin, chilli powder, couscous and boiling water. Cover with a plate and set aside for 8-10 minutes, then fluff with a fork and season with salt and pepper.
Toast the pistachios in a dry pan over a high heat for 2 minutes.
Spoon the couscous and jackfruit into bowls, garnish with coriander leaves, parsley, pistachios and pomegranate seeds and serve immediately, with hummus if you like.
